label: Credentials, keys and certificates
description: A secret in a document is a secret already leaked: it was written down, mailed, exported and is now being imported. Nothing else in this catalogue is as cheap to act on — a key that reaches the store is a key to rotate, whatever is decided about the file.

matchers.label: Private key block
matchers.hint: A PEM private key. Rotate it, whatever becomes of this file.

matchers.label: Certificate block
matchers.hint: A certificate is public by design; it is here because it says which hosts and which authority.

matchers.label: PKCS#12 / keystore passphrase
matchers.hint: A keystore named beside its passphrase.

matchers.label: AWS secret access key
matchers.hint: Forty characters of base64 under the name AWS gives it.

matchers.label: Model provider key
matchers.hint: The shape OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter all use.

matchers.label: JSON Web Token
matchers.hint: Anyone holding it is whoever it was issued to, until it expires.

matchers.label: Named secret assigned a value
matchers.hint: The .env shape: a name that means secret, an equals sign, and something long enough to be one.

matchers.label: Credentials inside a URL
matchers.hint: A connection string carrying its own user and password.

matchers.label: Password hash
matchers.hint: bcrypt, argon2 or a crypt(3) hash — an offline cracking target.

matchers.label: Private key file named
matchers.hint: The file is named, so the secret may be attached beside it.
